item.description:

During authorized security testing, certain crafted JavaScript and code-injection payloads were also observed to cause the embedded web interface to crash and become temporarily unavailable on some tested software versions. This behavior represents a denial-of-service condition affecting the embedded web management interface; no device-level denial of service was established.

item.title: CVE-2026-99804 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
io_uring/io-wq: save worker type before dropping its reference
io_wq_cancel_tw_create() inspects cb->func after calling io_worker_cancel_cb(). For an existing worker, that call can drop the last worker reference and wake io_worker_exit(). If the canceling task is preempted, the worker can be unlinked and freed by kfree_rcu() before the callback function is inspected. KASAN reports a slab-use-after-free read in this path.
Save whether the callback belongs to an unpublished continuation worker while its reference is still held, then use the saved result for the conditional free. This preserves the existing accounting and frees only the worker allocated for the canceled continuation.
Score: 7.8 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-99799
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
io_uring/sqpoll: don't wait for the thread to exit
io_sq_thread_stop() wakes the SQPOLL thread and waits for it to exit. The thread belongs to the thread group that created the ring, so a SIGSTOP or the cgroup freezer holds it in get_signal(), and the wake up doesn't change that. io_ring_exit_work() then sleeps in that wait until someone continues or kills the process. iou_exit has 64 slots, so 64 closed SQPOLL rings of a stopped process keep every other ring from being freed, for everyone.
Don't wait. Set the stop bit, wake the thread, and let it exit when it gets to run again. The sqd can now outlive its last ring, so give it a second refcount with one reference for the rings and one for the thread, and free it with the last one. The thread can't reach a freed ring, rings leave ctx_list before dropping their reference, and the io-wq hash is refcounted.

item.title: CVE-2026-99797
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
io_uring/cancel: drop sqd->lock while SQPOLL waits
An exiting SQPOLL thread calls io_uring_cancel_generic() with sqd->lock held, and keeps it across cond_resched() and the sleep until nothing is in flight anymore. A zero-copy send notification can't be canceled and stays pending as long as the peer doesn't read, so the lock is held for as long as a user cares to. io_ring_exit_work() needs it to park the thread, and so do IORING_REGISTER_IOWQ_AFF and IOWQ_MAX_WORKERS. With 64 such rings sharing the thread, every iou_exit slot sleeps on the lock and no ring gets freed for anyone.
Drop the lock around cond_resched() and the sleep, like the main loop of the thread does. Each walk of ctx_list is still under one hold, and nothing is kept across the unlock. The thread drops its io-wq, frees its tctx and clears sqd->thread under one hold after the loop, so whoever holds the lock and finds sqd->thread set can still use them.
[axboe: adapted to the schedule_timeout() based loop]

item.title: CVE-2026-99796
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
io_uring/poll: cancel all matching requests in one pass
With IORING_ASYNC_CANCEL_ALL, __io_async_cancel() calls io_try_cancel() until nothing is found, and io_poll_cancel() cancels one request per call, starting each lookup at the beginning of the hash. A cancelled request stays hashed until its task work runs, so every lookup walks past the ones already cancelled. Cancelling K of N pending polls visits about K*N/2 requests in one io_uring_enter(), with uring_lock held.
A single CANCEL_FD|ALL on 80000 polls on one eventfd takes 17.06s, 0.02s with this change. With voluntary preemption the soft lockup watchdog fires:
watchdog: BUG: soft lockup - CPU#1 stuck for 26s! [repro:100] RIP: 0010:io_cancel_req_match+0x19/0xa0 io_poll_cancel+0x73/0x170 io_try_cancel+0x7b/0xf0 __io_async_cancel+0x41/0x110
Walk the hash once and cancel every match, as io_cancel_remove() does for futex and waitid. Cancel by user_data only needs its own bucket. __io_async_cancel() still loops until nothing is found, so a request that io-wq parks in the poll hash meanwhile is still cancelled.
A cancel that matches one request now walks the whole hash twice instead of stopping at the match.

item.title: CVE-2026-99794 [CVSS:3.1 8.3 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
Bluetooth: L2CAP: Reject signalling responses in invalid states
A peer can send configuration messages while an incoming channel is in BT_CONNECT2, before the security or deferred accept gate has completed. A configuration response can then promote the channel to BT_CONNECTED. Configuration responses can also act on channels that are closing, and a late connection response can move a disconnecting channel back to BT_CONFIG.
Accept connection responses only while waiting in BT_CONNECT. Answer configuration requests in BT_CONNECT2, but defer our own request until BT_CONFIG so configuration cannot complete before the gate. Ignore configuration responses outside BT_CONFIG and BT_CONNECTED, and only complete configuration in BT_CONFIG.
Score: 8.3 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:A/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:L

item.title: CVE-2026-99793 [CVSS:3.1 8.1 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
Bluetooth: L2CAP: Only accept connection responses to outstanding requests
An outgoing channel waits in BT_CONNECT until security and the feature mask exchange complete, and only then sends its connection request. A peer can answer it before that with a connection response matching our source CID. The channel then moves to BT_CONFIG, completes configuration and becomes connected before security has completed. If security then fails, l2cap_security_cfm() leaves the connected channel alone, so it stays up on a link that did not reach the required security level.
A connection response with a zero source CID is matched by identifier. Another channel can hold the same identifier for a response it still has to send, so the lookup can pick the wrong channel.
Only accept a connection response while our request is outstanding, and only look at such channels when matching by identifier.
Score: 8.1 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:A/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N

item.title: CVE-2026-99788
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ACPI: CPPC: Validate FFH register fields before hardware access
The x86 CPPC FFH accessors construct masks and shift values using the firmware's Bit Width and Bit Offset without checking that the field fits in an MSR. A zero-width field or a field extending beyond bit 63 can therefore cause an invalid shift. The safe MSR accessors only handle an access fault, not invalid field arithmetic after a successful read.
Also, the 64-bit GAS address is implicitly narrowed to the 32-bit MSR number. A descriptor with nonzero upper address bits can access a different MSR from the one described by firmware.
The arm64 AMU counter readers have the same unchecked field arithmetic. Validate the field bounds before reading a counter, including both descriptors in the paired counter path.
Dispatch FFH accesses before decoding the GAS Access Size in the common read and write paths. Otherwise, a large access_width can trigger an invalid shift in GET_BIT_WIDTH() before the architecture validates its register. That field has architecture-specific FFH semantics and is not needed by the generic memory/port accessor on this path.
Validate x86 MSR addresses and share the field-bounds checks between related accessors within each architecture.

item.title: CVE-2026-99786
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
xfrm: retry inexact policy lookup after node reinsertion
An inexact policy lookup first records pointers to candidate hlist heads and then traverses the lists. A concurrent policy insertion can merge inexact tree nodes between those operations:
lookup policy insertion ------ ---------------- find inexact candidates save obsolete hlist head write_seqcount_begin(&bin->count) merge inexact tree nodes hlist_del_rcu(&policy->bydst) reinsert policy->bydst in survivor write_seqcount_end(&bin->count) evaluate saved candidate list miss the moved policy
The merge immediately reinserts the same hlist node into the surviving tree node. RCU keeps the policy alive, but it does not provide a consistent view while its list node is moved. A lookup that selected the obsolete list can observe it empty. A lookup already traversing a moved policy can instead follow the next pointer rewritten by the reinsertion. Either case can return an incorrect IPsec policy result.
The per-bin sequence counter already brackets calls to xfrm_policy_inexact_insert_node(), including node merges. The read side, however, currently validates the counter only while searching an individual rb-tree. A successful search returns without validation, and the later candidate-list traversal is outside that read-side section.
Snapshot the per-bin sequence before discovering candidate heads and validate it after evaluating all candidate lists. Retry the lookup if the inexact policy tree changes while it is being searched.
