item.title: CVE-2026-99785 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
9p/trans_virtio: reject mount tags longer than NAME_MAX at probe
p9_virtio_probe() reads a 16-bit mount tag length (tag_len) from the device config and kzalloc()s tag_len + 1 bytes for chan->tag with no upper bound. A malicious or compromised host can present a tag of up to 65535 bytes; that tag is later copied into the single-page sysfs buffer by p9_mount_tag_show() (memcpy(buf, chan->tag, tag_len + 1)), a host-controlled out-of-bounds write of up to ~64 KiB past the PAGE_SIZE attribute buffer.
Reject an overlong tag at probe time. A 9p mount tag is a name-like identifier, so bound it by NAME_MAX (255): that limit is independent of the sysfs/seq_file page size and is far above any legitimate mount tag, which keeps p9_mount_tag_show() safe at the root without hard-coding a seq_file implementation detail.
Score: 7.8 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-99784
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
9p/xen: fix refcount leak in p9_xen_response() on wrong tag
p9_xen_response() looks up the request for an incoming reply with p9_tag_lookup(), which takes a reference on the returned p9_req_t. When the tag does not resolve to a request in REQ_STATUS_SENT, the function warns and continues the loop without dropping that reference, permanently leaking the p9_req_t and its msize buffers. The reply header, including the tag, is supplied by the backend, so a malicious or buggy 9P backend can leak kernel memory on every crafted response.
Drop the reference before continuing.

item.title: CVE-2026-99775
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
xfrm: interface: validate the IP header on xmit
Packets injected into an xfrm interface (e.g. AF_PACKET on an xfrmi device) reach the xfrm output path without IP header validation, but xfrm4_transport_output() uses iph->ihl for __skb_pull() and memmove() and expects the header to be valid.
vti_tunnel_xmit() already calls pskb_inet_may_pull() before handing packets to the xfrm output path. Do the same in xfrmi_xmit() and perform the header checks ip_rcv_core()/ip6_rcv_core() do on entry to the IP stack: reject wrong IP versions and malformed IPv4 header lengths.

item.title: CVE-2026-99774
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
xfrm: espintcp: reorder operations within espintcp_init_sk
When enabled on a socket, espintcp sets the socket callbacks to its own before it has finished setting up its context and published it as icsk_ulp_data. Any one of those callbacks that gets called before will dereference a NULL icsk_ulp_data.
Fix this by reording the operations, and add memory barriers to ensure callers will have a struct espintcp_ctx available. Add a few WRITE_ONCE/READ_ONCE too while we're there.

item.title: CVE-2026-99773 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
drm/drm_crtc: ensure dma_fence_ops remain valid during device unbind
In [1], sashiko reported the following issue:
=== snip === Looking at how these fences are managed, drm_crtc_create_fence() creates a dma_fence without taking a reference to the drm_device or drm_crtc. Because the sync_file framework exposes this fence to userspace, the fence can outlive the CRTC.
The dma_fence contract requires that data accessed by dma_fence_ops (like get_driver_name) must remain valid for an RCU grace period after the fence is signaled. However, drm_crtc_cleanup() and the subsequent freeing of the device do not wait for an RCU grace period via synchronize_rcu().
If userspace calls ioctl(SYNC_IOC_FILE_INFO) concurrently with a device hot-unplug:
CPU1 (Userspace) sync_file_get_name() ops = rcu_dereference(fence->ops); if (!dma_fence_test_signaled_flag()) // Preempted or delayed here
CPU2 (Driver Teardown) Signals the fence (setting fence->ops = NULL) Destroys and frees the CRTC without waiting for an RCU grace period
CPU1 (Resumes) ops->get_driver_name(fence) -> drm_crtc_fence_get_driver_name() crtc = fence_to_crtc(fence); // Casts to the freed CRTC return crtc->dev->driver->name; // Use-after-free
...
Does the CRTC or DRM device need to be kept alive for the RCU grace period, or should the fence hold a proper reference to prevent the use-after-free when get_driver_name() and get_timeline_name() access the freed CRTC structure? === snap ===
I believe this to be a correct observation and this patch implements the suggestion of waiting for an RCU grace period before proceeding with destruction of the drm_crtc, so that get_driver_name() and get_timeline_name() can still work.
Score: 7.8 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-99771
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
wifi: mac80211: reload TDLS header pointer after skb_linearize()
ieee80211_process_tdls_channel_switch() sets tf = skb->data before it calls skb_linearize(), and reads tf->action_code afterwards.
ieee80211_rx_h_data() queues TDLS channel switch requests and responses to the interface after pulling only offsetof(struct ieee80211_tdls_data, u) bytes, so the skb can still be non-linear when the interface work handles it. Drivers that build paged RX skbs do this for every frame that does not fit into the skb head, e.g. iwlwifi (mvm), which is also the only mac80211 driver that sets NL80211_FEATURE_TDLS_CHANNEL_SWITCH. If the remaining data does not fit into the tailroom, skb_linearize() moves the data to a new head and frees the old one, and the action code is then read from freed memory. Depending on what that memory holds by then, the frame is handled as before or ends in the WARN_ON_ONCE() of the default case.
The frame only has to be a data frame with the TDLS ethertype from an authorized peer, e.g. relayed by the AP from another station in the BSS; the read happens before the sender is checked to be a TDLS peer.
Load tf after skb_linearize(), as the request and response handlers already do.
Found by static analysis tool CodeQL.

item.title: CVE-2026-99770
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
drm/vc4: Publish the output fence outside of job_lock
job_lock is taken by the V3D interrupt handler, so nesting an IRQ-unsafe lock under it creates an inversion. drm_syncobj_replace_fence() takes drm_syncobj::lock, which other paths acquire with interrupts enabled. For example, a thread interrupted while holding it blocks the handler on job_lock, and the handler can only make progress once the submit path releases job_lock, which it cannot do while waiting for drm_syncobj::lock.
This is reported by lockdep:
[ 188.139076] ======================================================== [ 188.139086] WARNING: possible irq lock inversion dependency detected [ 188.139096] 7.3.0-rc3-00067-gc4f3feeaf60f #67 Tainted: G C [ 188.139108] -------------------------------------------------------- [ 188.139116] swapper/0/0 just changed the state of lock: [ 188.139125] ffff0000054f8ff8 (&vc4->job_lock){-...}-{3:3}, at: vc4_irq+0xa8/0x28c [vc4] [ 188.139234] but this lock took another, HARDIRQ-unsafe lock in the past: [ 188.139242] (&syncobj->lock){+.+.}-{3:3} [ 188.139256] and interrupts could create inverse lock ordering between them. [ 188.139267] other info that might help us debug this: [ 188.139275] Possible interrupt unsafe locking scenario: [ 188.139284] CPU0 CPU1 [ 188.139291] ---- ---- [ 188.139299] lock(&syncobj->lock); [ 188.139312] local_irq_disable(); [ 188.139320] lock(&vc4->job_lock); [ 188.139335] lock(&syncobj->lock); [ 188.139350] <Interrupt> [ 188.139358] lock(&vc4->job_lock); [ 188.139372] *** DEADLOCK ***
Hand the fence over after job_lock is dropped. The job can complete and drop exec->fence in that window, so take a reference first and publish through the local pointer, as exec may already be gone.

item.title: CVE-2026-99768
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
wifi: mac80211: reinstate IEEE80211_TX_CTL_AMPDU flag in ieee80211_tx_prep_agg()
The commit 592234e941f1 ("wifi: mac80211: Fix iTXQ AMPDU fragmentation handling") changed the way handling of the IEEE80211_TX_CTL_AMPDU flag is done in mac80211, so the only place it is set is in ieee80211_tx_dequeue().
This means that any frames that are sent to the driver via drv_tx() will no longer have the flag set. In particular, this affects packets going through ieee80211_tx_pending(). Evan reported that this can result in the ath9k driver failing to account such packets in its block ack window, eventually overrunning the window and stalling TX.
Fix this by reinstating the flag in ieee80211_tx_prep_agg() when inside a valid block ack window. This should be harmless for the TXQ path, and will reinstate the previous behaviour for drivers that use the flag as a signal to track the packet in the window.

item.title: CVE-2026-99765
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
scsi: target: Fix demo-mode dynamic ACL dev-entry UAF vs LUN teardown
A demo-mode (generate_node_acls=1) login that allocates a dynamic NodeACL populates that ACL's per-LUN dev entries in core_tpg_add_node_to_devs() *before* the ACL is linked onto tpg->acl_node_list by target_add_node_acl():
core_tpg_check_initiator_node_acl(): ... core_tpg_add_node_to_devs(acl, tpg, NULL); /* builds deves */ target_add_node_acl(acl); /* only now listed */
The LUN teardown sweep, core_clear_lun_from_tpg(), enumerates only tpg->acl_node_list, so a dev entry whose ACL is still in the window above is invisible to the sweep and is never disabled. It is left on the se_lun->lun_deve_list after core_tpg_remove_lun() frees the se_lun; when the same unpacked_lun is later re-added and the se_lun is reallocated at the same address, the stale dev entry is rediscovered by target_nacl_find_deve() and core_enable_device_list_for_node() corrupts lun_deve_list:
BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free ... core_enable_device_list_for_node+0x5ce/0x880 core_tpg_add_node_to_devs+0x169/0x190 core_dev_add_lun+0x146/0x190 target_fabric_port_link+0xe9/0x1b0 configfs_symlink+0x381/0xae0 __x64_sys_symlink+0x55/0x80
The demo-mode login path that drives the ACL/dev-entry creation is reachable by an unauthenticated initiator; the colliding LUN add/remove is a local configfs operation.
Commit 49cb77e297dc ("target: Avoid mappedlun symlink creation during lun shutdown") introduced se_lun->lun_shutdown and guarded the *explicit* ACL MappedLUN path (target_fabric_mappedlun_link()), but the demo-mode automatic path, core_tpg_add_node_to_devs() -> core_enable_device_list_for_node(), was never given the equivalent guard, and the publish-after-populate ordering in core_tpg_check_initiator_node_acl() was left unchanged.
Fix it in three cooperating parts:
1) Publish the dynamic NodeACL onto acl_node_list *before* creating its dev entries, so the teardown sweep can observe them.
2) Refuse to attach a dev entry to an se_lun that is shutting down, checked under nacl->lun_entry_mutex -- the same lock the sweep takes -- so once the sweep has passed an ACL any later enable for that LUN observes lun_shutdown and skips it.
3) In core_enable_device_list_for_node(), insert the new dev entry onto lun->lun_deve_list while still holding nacl->lun_entry_mutex, in both the replace and the new-entry branch. Previously the entry was added to nacl->lun_entry_hlist under the mutex but to lun->lun_deve_list only after dropping it; with the ACL now published early, the sweep could take the mutex in that gap, find the entry on the hlist, core_disable_device_list_for_node() it (list_del() on the not-yet- linked lun_link succeeds and the entry is freed), and then the enable would list_add_tail() the freed entry back onto lun_deve_list. Linking both lists under the mutex makes enable and the sweep mutually exclusive, closing that window.
core_tpg_add_node_to_devs() already ignores the return value of core_enable_device_list_for_node(), so a shutting-down LUN is simply skipped.

item.title: CVE-2026-99764
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
9p/xen: validate the response size from the backend
p9_xen_response() takes the length of an incoming response from the ring -- the first field of the 9p header, which the Xen transport reuses as its framing header -- and uses it to advance the consumer index, but never checks that it is at least the header size or no larger than the number of bytes the backend has actually produced.
A malicious or buggy backend can post a response whose size is smaller than the header (for example 0). The consumer index then never advances, so the response work re-reads the same ring contents instead of making progress. In testing this raced with the teardown that the malformed reply triggers and dereferenced a freed p9_client:
9pfs 9pfs-0: Wrong req tag=ffff BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000060 #PF: supervisor read access in kernel mode #PF: error_code(0x0000) - not-present page PGD 0 P4D 0 Oops: Oops: 0000 [#1] SMP NOPTI CPU: 0 UID: 0 PID: 11 Comm: kworker/0:1 Not tainted 7.2.0-rc5 #6 PREEMPT(lazy) Hardware name: QEMU Standard PC (Q35 + ICH9, 2009), BIOS rel-1.17.0-0-gb52ca86e094d-prebuilt.qemu.org 04/01/2014 Workqueue: events p9_xen_response RIP: 0010:idr_find+0x4/0x10 RSP: 0018:ffffbf5d80063de8 EFLAGS: 00010202 RAX: 0000000000000001 RBX: ffffa229c21195a0 RCX: ffffa229c2400000 RDX: ffffa229c11c2200 RSI: 000000000000ffff RDI: 0000000000000050 RBP: 000000000000ffff R08: 3fffffffffffdfff R09: ffffffffffffffff R10: 3fffffffffffdfff R11: ffffffff87a60e80 R12: 0000000000000050 R13: 0000000000000000 R14: 000000000000ffff R15: 0000000000100000 FS: 0000000000000000(0000) GS:ffffa22a7661c000(0000) knlGS:0000000000000000 CS: 0010 DS: 0000 ES: 0000 CR0: 0000000080050033 CR2: 0000000000000060 CR3: 000000003ac34002 CR4: 0000000000770ef0 PKRU: 55555554 Call Trace: <TASK> p9_tag_lookup+0x2b/0x90 p9_xen_response+0x17c/0x2e0 process_one_work+0x16a/0x3a0 worker_thread+0x172/0x2e0 kthread+0xdd/0x110 ret_from_fork+0x18b/0x240 ret_from_fork_asm+0x1a/0x30 </TASK> Modules linked in: CR2: 0000000000000060 ---[ end trace 0000000000000000 ]---
Reject a response whose size is outside [sizeof(header), queued] before using it, matching the validation the backend already applies to incoming requests.

item.title: CVE-2026-99763
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
9p: don't decrement a server-owned zero nlink
A 9P2000.L server can report nlink=0 for a regular file that still exists. On a cache=loose or cache=fscache mount, lookup stores that value with set_nlink(). A later successful unlink calls v9fs_dec_count(), which still calls drop_nlink() for a non-directory. drop_nlink() warns, and the unsigned link count wraps to 4294967295. fstat() on a descriptor opened before the unlink shows 0 before and 4294967295 after.
The warning on the unpatched kernel, trimmed:
WARNING: fs/inode.c:408 at drop_nlink+0xac/0xd0, CPU#1: trigger/188 CPU: 1 UID: 0 PID: 188 Comm: trigger Tainted: G N 7.3.0-rc4-00537-ga3ff15db6820 #1 PREEMPT(lazy) RIP: 0010:drop_nlink+0xac/0xd0 Call Trace: <TASK> v9fs_remove+0x529/0x750 vfs_unlink+0x2f0/0xbd0 filename_unlinkat+0x340/0x6c0 __x64_sys_unlink+0x46/0x70 do_syscall_64+0xe8/0x4f0 entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x77/0x7f </TASK> ---[ end trace 0000000000000000 ]---
Directories whose cached nlink is at most 2 already skip this decrement, because the exported filesystem may not maintain nlink (commit ac89b2ef9b559). cache=none skips it as well (commit 574aa0b479947). cache=mmap does not take this path: it sets neither CACHE_META nor CACHE_LOOSE. A regular file on cache=loose or cache=fscache still does. Its count came from GETATTR and may already be zero, so skip the decrement when i_nlink is already 0.
Verified on 7.3-rc4-00537-ga3ff15db6820 with only this change. A server that advertises nlink=0 and accepts the unlink no longer warns, and the open descriptor stays at nlink 0. An honest server on the same mount still goes from 1 to 0. A rejected unlink leaves the count unchanged. cache=none is unchanged. With panic_on_warn the unpatched kernel panics on the warning; the patched kernel does not.

item.title: CVE-2026-99761 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
batman-adv: stop originator purge worker before freeing TT
batadv_mesh_free() releases the translation tables via batadv_tt_free() before batadv_originator_free() stops orig_work. The purge worker can therefore still run while the TT is torn down. When an originator times out, batadv_purge_orig_ref() calls batadv_tt_global_del_orig(), which loads tt.global_hash and walks all buckets while taking their locks:
CPU0 CPU1 batadv_tt_free() batadv_purge_orig() batadv_tt_global_del_orig() hash = ...tt.global_hash; batadv_tt_global_table_free() batadv_hash_destroy(hash); spin_lock_bh(&hash->list_locks[i]);
Disable orig_work at the beginning of batadv_mesh_free(), directly after the mesh was marked as deactivating. The second disable_delayed_work_sync() in batadv_originator_free() is harmless because it is free'd anyway.
Score: 7.8 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-99760 [CVSS:3.1 7.6 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
batman-adv: tt: ignore ROAM flag of received ADD changes
A received TT change (OGM diff or full table response) with the ROAM flag but without DEL is handled by batadv_tt_global_add() like a ROAMING_ADV:
* a newly created global entry gets BATADV_TT_CLIENT_ROAM and is therefore excluded from the global CRC. The sender has it in its local CRC and the receiver has to request the full table again * batadv_tt_global_purge_local() removes the local entry of the receiver. The receiver's own client is considered as roamed to the sender and frames for it are rerouted
The ROAM flag only has a meaning together with DEL. Drop it on reception to keep it from populating the global table with a temporary ROAMING entry which is not part of the CRC - and therefore causing a CRC mismatch.
Score: 7.6 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:A/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-99759
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
batman-adv: tt: don't drop local events queued during TVLV update
batadv_tt_tvlv_container_update() read the number of local changes without holding changes_list_lock. batadv_tt_local_event() is not serialized by the commit_lock and can queue new events before the changes_list is flushed:
CPU0 CPU1 batadv_tt_tvlv_container_update() num = ...local_changes; batadv_tt_local_event() list_add_tail(...); ...local_changes++; spin_lock_bh(&...changes_list_lock); /* only num events copied but all freed */
The additional events were freed without ever being sent. Other nodes will only notice this via a CRC mismatch and must request the full table.
The number of changes and the changes_list must therefore be taken atomically. Events queued afterwards then stay in the tt.changes_list for the next TT round.
The changes can no longer be kept for the next round when the TVLV buffer allocation fails. But they would be sent with a skipped TTVN anyway, so the other nodes have to request the full table in this case either way. The last changeset is only dropped in this case when the TTVN was incremented. Without new changes, it still describes the current TTVN.
Previously, the unconsumed changes caused a retry of the TVLV container update in the next commit round. Since the changes are now consumed, the next round would only take the path without changes and wait for BATADV_TT_OGM_APPEND_MAX rounds before updating the container again. Until then, the outdated container with the previous TTVN would still be announced. The ogm_append_cnt is therefore reset on failure to retry the update in the next OGM interval.
This doesn't make the CRC consistent with the announced changeset. The local table modifications are still not serialized with the commit and batadv_tt_local_transition_new() can still make a client part of the CRC for which the event is only part of the next TT round. Such an inconsistency is detected by the CRC check of the other nodes and solved via a full table request.

item.title: CVE-2026-99758 [CVSS:3.1 7.5 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
sctp: account for chunk padding in sctp_init_cause()
sctp_init_cause() accepts a chunk when skb_tailroom() can hold the cause header and the payload. sctp_addto_chunk() then writes 0-3 bytes of padding before that header so the chunk stays 4-byte aligned. The check does not include the padding, and the following skb_put() calls skb_over_panic() from softirq.
Count the padding sctp_addto_chunk() is about to write. The cause length on the wire stays the header plus the payload.
Found by LLM inspection, triggered and tested the fix.
Score: 7.5 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-99757
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
btrfs: sysfs: restore NOFS context on early return in btrfs_sysfs_add_block_group_type()
btrfs_sysfs_add_block_group_type() sets up a NOFS context with memalloc_nofs_save() because kobject_add() performs GFP_KERNEL allocations deep in its call chain, and the function may be called while holding a transaction handle or a lock required for a transaction commit, where reclaim could deadlock.
Every other return path of this function calls memalloc_nofs_restore() except the early return taken when another thread has already created the kobject for the same raid index (this can happen when restriping). Taking that path leaves PF_MEMALLOC_NOFS set on the calling task, so all subsequent memory allocations performed by that task remain restricted to the NOFS scope, which may lead to unexpected allocation failures or deadlocks later on.
Restore the NOFS context before returning from that path.

item.title: CVE-2026-99756
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
btrfs: prevent deleting the wrong subvolume by ID
When deleting a subvolume by ID, btrfs_ioctl_snap_destroy() first resolves the requested ID to a name, then looks up that name again under the parent directory lock.
A concurrent rename can change which subvolume is associated with the name between these operations. Since the deletion path does not verify the ID of the resolved subvolume, it can delete a different subvolume while leaving the requested one intact.
This was reproduced by repeatedly exchanging the names of two subvolumes using renameat2(RENAME_EXCHANGE) while deleting one of them by ID. The wrong subvolume was deleted in 9 out of 14 independent tests.
Fix this by checking that the resolved subvolume ID matches the requested ID while holding the parent directory lock. Return -EAGAIN on a mismatch so that userspace can retry the operation instead of being told that the requested subvolume does not exist.

item.title: CVE-2026-99754 [CVSS:3.1 7.1 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
scsi: target: Verify the iSCSI ISID is null-terminated
iscsi_parse_pr_out_transport_id() returns the ISID of a FORMAT CODE 01b TransportID as a pointer into the PERSISTENT RESERVE OUT parameter list, lowercased in place and never null-terminated. spc4r37 Table 508 requires the field to be null-terminated, but a non-conforming initiator can omit the NULL; when the ISID ends at the end of the received buffer, the pointer is not a C string.
The registration code still consumes it as one: strcmp() in __core_scsi3_locate_pr_reg() and in the REGISTER AND MOVE path, and snprintf("%s") in __core_scsi3_do_alloc_registration(), which also reads its first 8 bytes unconditionally with get_unaligned_be64() - a NUL check does not bound that read.
When the parameter list spans more than one page, transport_kmap_data_sg() maps it with vmap(), and the over-read walks off the end of the mapping into the vmalloc() guard page and oopses. Reproduced with a PR OUT REGISTER + SPEC_I_PT parameter list of exactly 8192 bytes whose final TransportID carries a 12-byte ISID without a terminating NUL:
BUG: unable to handle page fault for address: ffffc9000138c000 RIP: 0010:strcmp+0xc/0x30 Call Trace: __core_scsi3_locate_pr_reg+0xd3/0x120 [target_core_mod] core_scsi3_decode_spec_i_port+0x8fc/0x13a0 [target_core_mod] core_scsi3_emulate_pro_register+0x73c/0x900 [target_core_mod] ... iscsi_target_rx_thread+0xef/0x1d0 [iscsi_target_mod]
With a single-page parameter list the buffer is a kmap() direct mapping, so the over-read continues into the physically adjacent page instead of faulting. snprintf("%s") then copies whatever follows the ISID in memory into pr_reg_isid, and PR IN READ FULL STATUS reports the registration back to any initiator, turning the over-read into an info leak of kernel heap contents. Reproduced with a 4096-byte parameter list whose last TransportID ends at the end of the buffer with a 4-byte ISID and no NUL, interleaved with I/O to populate adjacent pages: the READ FULL STATUS response returned the ISID as "0xleak" followed by raw bytes that were not part of the parameter list. The snprintf() into pr_reg_isid[PR_REG_ISID_LEN] caps the echoed ISID at 15 characters, so at most 11 bytes past the buffer are leaked per command, but the PR OUT command is not rate limited.
Any initiator that can send PR OUT to an iSCSI-exported LUN can trigger either variant, including a guest via vhost-scsi.
Require 8 bytes to remain after the ",i,0x" separator, and a NUL inside the rest of the descriptor, before the ISID pointer is returned. REGISTER AND MOVE fails with TCM_INVALID_PARAMETER_LIST; on SPEC_I_PT no target port claims the malformed TransportID, and the command fails the same way.
Score: 7.1 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-99753 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
drm/loongson: Fix double free on BO initialization failure
If ttm_bo_init_validate() fails, it drops the buffer object's reference and cleans it up through the supplied destroy callback. lsdc_bo_destroy() releases the GEM object and frees the enclosing lsdc_bo, so freeing it again in lsdc_bo_create() causes a double free on a synchronous failure path.
Let TTM own the cleanup after initialization has started and return the error directly. Keep the explicit free on drm_gem_object_init() failure, which occurs before ownership is passed to TTM.
Tested on LS7A2000 by making drm_vma_offset_add() return -ENOSPC for one selected dumb-buffer creation. The error reached userspace, the destroy callback ran once, and no handle was published or tracked BO retained. Normal buffer creation, zeroing, mapping, readback and release passed.
AI assistance was used for the ownership analysis, fix, fault-injection tools, build and test execution.
Score: 7.8 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-99752
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
drm/loongson: Handle buffer mapping failures when clearing a BO
lsdc_bo_clear() ignores the return value from lsdc_bo_kmap() and writes to lbo->kptr unconditionally. When the first mapping of a newly allocated buffer fails, kptr is still NULL and the subsequent memset accesses it.
Return the mapping error without touching the buffer and propagate it from lsdc_gem_object_create(). Install the GEM object functions before clearing so that drm_gem_object_put() can release the buffer correctly on failure. Do not add the failed object to the tracking list or return an uncleared buffer to the caller.
Imported buffers still skip clearing, and successfully mapped buffers are cleared and unmapped as before.
Tested on LS7A2000 with a one-shot range error in ttm_bo_kmap(). Its -EINVAL return reached userspace, the object was destroyed once, and no GEM handle was published. Normal create/map/zero/write/read/close cycles passed, with the tracked BO count and VRAM usage unchanged.
AI assistance was used for the lifetime analysis, fix, fault-injection tools, build and test execution.

item.title: CVE-2026-99751
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
bpf: Fix skb_pull() BUG in __bpf_redirect_neigh()
The issue: This is a follow-up to the short link-layer header fixes from Eric. After vlan pop_eth, a privileged SCHED_ACT BPF program can call bpf_skb_change_head(skb, 1, 0) and then bpf_redirect_neigh().
__bpf_redirect_neigh() calls skb_pull(skb, sizeof(*ethh)) after checking only that mac_header < network_header. Nothing verifies that the MAC header is long enough, that it is linear, or that the IP header the redirect goes on to read is linear either.
A SCHED_ACT BPF program can do:
bpf_skb_change_head(skb, 1, 0); bpf_redirect_neigh(lo, NULL, 0, 0);
after vlan pop_eth. The skb then has mac_len == 1 and only one byte of linear data; skb_pull(ETH_HLEN) trips the skb->len < skb->data_len BUG in __skb_pull():
kernel BUG at ./include/linux/skbuff.h:2839! RIP: skb_pull+0x40/0x50 Call Trace: skb_do_redirect -> packet_xmit -> packet_sendmsg Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception in interrupt
The v4 and v6 paths read ip_hdr() and ipv6_hdr() as soon as the MAC header is gone. On the AF_PACKET frame below that leaves headlen == 0 after the pull, so the network header sits at skb->tail and the route lookup reads ip4h->protocol, ip4h->saddr and ip4h->daddr past the linear area.
The Fix: Use skb_network_offset(), which is the MAC header span, instead of skb->mac_len. mac_len is zero for locally generated tc egress and netkit packets, while the span still rejects the one-byte header produced by pop_eth + bpf_skb_change_head(skb, 1, 0). The single check also covers the mac_header >= network_header test it replaces.
Use pskb_may_pull() to make the Ethernet header linear before it is read or pulled, and to make the IP header linear in both the v4 and the v6 path before ip_hdr()/ipv6_hdr() is read. The header pointers are taken after the pull, since pskb_may_pull() may reallocate skb->head.
Conditions to recreate the bug: On x86-64 with 4 KiB pages, enable CONFIG_PACKET, CONFIG_BPF_SYSCALL, CONFIG_NET_SCH_INGRESS, CONFIG_NET_CLS_MATCHALL, CONFIG_NET_ACT_VLAN and CONFIG_NET_ACT_BPF. Run as root with BPF loading, network administration and raw-packet privileges. Bring lo up and attach a SCHED_ACT program that calls bpf_skb_change_head(skb, 1, 0), then returns bpf_redirect_neigh(skb->ifindex, NULL, 0, 0):
ip link set lo up tc qdisc add dev lo clsact tc filter add dev lo egress matchall action vlan pop_eth pipe \ action bpf object-file neigh_chghead.o section action
Send an untagged ETH_P_IP frame of ETH_HLEN + 8192 bytes through an AF_PACKET/SOCK_RAW socket bound to lo, without PACKET_VNET_HDR or PACKET_QDISC_BYPASS. Use a unicast destination MAC. The sender's skb has a 14-byte linear Ethernet prefix and a fragmented payload; pop_eth removes that prefix and change_head restores only one linear byte. The unfixed neighbor redirect then tries to pull 14 bytes and BUGs.
Sending the same frame without pop_eth and change_head leaves the IP header in the frags, which is the route lookup reading past skb->tail.

item.title: CVE-2026-99750
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ksmbd: require DELETE access for delete-on-close opens
smb2_open() accepts FILE_DELETE_ON_CLOSE on an existing file without DELETE in DesiredAccess. When the request asks only for FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES or READ_CONTROL, it also skips inode_permission() and the parent directory MAY_WRITE | MAY_EXEC check that delete-on-close is meant to get. The file is then marked for deletion by a caller who could not delete it.
The unlink happens later, in __ksmbd_inode_close(), when the last handle on the inode is closed, and it runs with the credentials of that handle. If the caller closes last, the unlink fails. If another user who can write the parent directory, such as the file's owner, still has the file open, the file is deleted when that user closes it. Until then new opens of the file fail with STATUS_DELETE_PENDING. So a user with only search permission on a directory can delete a file in it, or block opens of it, while the owner has it open.
A MAXIMUM_ALLOWED open that also requests DELETE has the same problem. The requested access is replaced with the maximal access, which does not include DELETE when the caller cannot write the parent directory, and the later permission checks are skipped as already done.
MS-FSA 2.1.5.1 requires an open with FILE_DELETE_ON_CLOSE and without DELETE in DesiredAccess to fail with STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER, and Samba does the same. Add that check to the CreateOptions validation, using the generic-mapped DesiredAccess so that GENERIC_ALL still qualifies. This also refuses MAXIMUM_ALLOWED with FILE_DELETE_ON_CLOSE but no explicit DELETE, as MS-FSA and Samba do. When MAXIMUM_ALLOWED is requested with DELETE but the maximal access does not include DELETE, fail with STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED. With DELETE requested, delete-on-close opens go through the existing parent directory check.

item.title: CVE-2026-99749
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ksmbd: enforce the read-only share flag when creating a stream
When a share is read-only, smb2_open() rejects opens that would create or truncate a file. Creating a named stream on an existing file with streams_xattr sets neither O_CREAT nor O_TRUNC, so it passes this check, and smb2_set_stream_name_xattr() then creates the stream. On a Time Machine share, opening a missing AFP_AfpInfo stream also writes one. A user who can write a file at the filesystem level can therefore add streams to it through a read-only share.
Do not create a stream or synthesize AFP_AfpInfo when the share is not writable. Existing streams still open normally, and a missing stream opened with FILE_OPEN still returns STATUS_OBJECT_NAME_NOT_FOUND.

item.title: CVE-2026-99748
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ksmbd: revert fsids on durable reconnect and replay failure
On a durable handle reconnect or a request replay, smb2_open() switches to the SMB user's fsids before calling ksmbd_vfs_getattr(). If that call fails, the code jumps to err_out2 and skips ksmbd_revert_fsids() at err_out1. The user's credentials then stay installed on the shared ksmbd worker. Later work on that worker, including other users' requests, runs with the first user's fsuid, fsgid and supplementary groups. ksmbd_free_work_struct() also warns, because work->saved_cred is still set.
Jump to err_out1 instead. No path is held at this point, so skipping the path_put() at err_out is correct.

item.title: CVE-2026-99746 [CVSS:3.1 7 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ASoC: SOF: Intel: hda-sdw-bpt: Stop active DMA before closing BPT streams
When sdw_enable_stream() fails in intel_ace2x_bpt_send_async() after hda_sdw_bpt_send_async() has already started the TX and RX DMA streams, intel_ace2x_bpt_close_stream() invokes hda_sdw_bpt_close() directly without calling hda_sdw_bpt_wait(). As a result, hda_sdw_bpt_dma_deprepare() tears down the DMA buffers and BDL while the DMA hardware is still running.
Disable any running TX or RX BPT DMA stream at the start of hda_sdw_bpt_close() before unmapping channels and depreparing DMA resources.
Score: 7 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-99744 [CVSS:3.1 7.1 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
net: atl1c: drop oversized RX frames instead of panicking
atl1c sizes its receive buffers from the netdev MTU plus a fixed set of L2 overheads, which comes to 1522 bytes at the default MTU. A link partner that sends a longer frame - in practice a MikroTik CCR2004-1G-2XS-PCIe, whose RouterOS side defaults to l2mtu 1600 while the host stays at MTU 1500 - makes the length reported by the RX return descriptor exceed what the hardware wrote, and skb_put() then either includes bytes that were never received or trips skb_over_panic and takes the host down.
Compare the descriptor length against buffer_info->length, the length the hardware was given, rather than against skb_tailroom(): the skb carries 64 bytes of slack for the DMA erratum, so tailroom is larger than the DMA buffer and a frame in between would pass the check and still be delivered with a tail the device never wrote. The same test rejects frames shorter than ETH_HLEN + ETH_FCS_LEN; before this change a reported length below ETH_FCS_LEN underflowed in skb_put().
The frame is dropped with kfree_skb_reason(SKB_DROP_REASON_PKT_TOO_BIG) so drop_monitor and the kfree_skb tracepoint see it, and counted through dev_core_stats_rx_dropped_inc(), which survives atl1c_get_stats() overwriting the hardware counters on every read. It also counts as work: atl1c_clean_rfd() has already recycled the RFD, and the refill at the end of the poll only runs when work_done is non-zero, so sustained oversized traffic would otherwise drain the ring and stop RX.
Tested on a MikroTik CCR2004-1G-2XS-PCIe (4x AR8151) in a Proxmox VE host, with atl1c built from a DKMS tree carrying this change: the l2mtu-1600 traffic that panics the stock driver is dropped and counted with the patch applied, and received normally once the host MTU is raised to match.
This complements commit 36c2009d90f2 ("net: atl1c: fix soft lockup on out-of-range tpd_cons read"), which fixed the TX side of the same "host dies while the card resets" problem.
Score: 7.1 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:A/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-99743
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ksmbd: grant a POSIX ACL group entry only to the group's members
When no ACE of the DACL matches the caller, Everyone or Authenticated Users, smb_check_perm_dacl() falls back to the file's POSIX ACL. It takes the first ACL_USER or ACL_GROUP entry whose id equals the caller's uid. For ACL_GROUP, this compares a gid with the caller's uid. A numerical match grants the group's permissions even when the caller is not a member.
Match a group entry only when the caller is also in the group.

item.title: CVE-2026-99742
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
mm/mempolicy: charge shared policy nodes
Any local user can bypass memory.max with mbind() on a tmpfs file, and allocate unbounded kernel memory.
mbind() sets a NUMA memory policy for a range of a mapping. If the mapping is of a shmem and friends, the kernel also stores the policy on the inode, in a tree with one entry per range of the file.
Each mbind() on a single page of a mapping can add one shared policy node (struct sp_node) and one struct mempolicy to that tree. They outlive the mapping and stay around until the inode is destroyed. The tree is not bounded by the file size, so the file can be empty.
Memory that user space can allocate must be charged to a memory cgroup. A slab cache does that for all of its objects if it is created with SLAB_ACCOUNT. numa_policy_init() creates the slab caches for both structs without SLAB_ACCOUNT, so they are not charged to any cgroup.
Reproduced with mbind() on single pages of an empty tmpfs file, from a cgroup with memory.max=8M: the global OOM killer killed tasks owned by root, and the machine panicked.
Fix this by creating both caches with SLAB_ACCOUNT. This change implies that mbind() can now fail when running into memcg limits. Further, the policy_cache also serves task and VMA policies, so they are similarly accounted now.
Note that per-file limits are not really helpful, as the user could simply use many files; having limits per user is tricky as well.
Fix generated by an LLM and submitted by Chris Mason in private.
[ david: smaller description tweaks ]

item.title: CVE-2026-99741
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
tmpfs: keep the quota soft limits of an unused id
When the last reference to a dquot goes away, shmem_release_dquot() stores its limits in the rb tree of the mount, unless shmem_is_empty_dquot() says that there is nothing worth storing. That function looks at the usage and at the two hard limits only.
So if the administrator sets nothing but soft limits for an id that owns no file yet, the entry is thrown away as soon as the dquot that Q_SETQUOTA used is released, and the id never gets to see a limit.
To fix it, compare the soft limits as well: an entry can be empty only if both soft limits are zero as well, which is exactly what shmem_acquire_dquot() sets for a new entry.
Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private.
[ david: slightly adjusted description ]

item.title: CVE-2026-99740
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
mm/shmem: stop retrying folios that cannot be split
A fault or collapse can insert a large folio crossing EOF after shmem_undo_range() has handled the boundary folios. If splitting that folio fails, truncate_inode_partial_folio() retains it when it is dirty. The final scan then repeatedly finds it because it restarts from an unchanged start.
Truncation keeps the inode lock and ignores fatal signals while looping. A concurrent unlink() can then block other directory operations while holding the directory lock and waiting for the file's lock.
Advance start past the retained folio, whose truncated part has already been zeroed. Do not move start backwards if the failed split has shrunk the folio.
Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private.
[ david: split fixes, simplify descriptions, adjust comments ]

item.title: CVE-2026-99738
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
mm/shmem: preserve allocation errors when swapping in large entries
shmem_swapin_folio() adjusts swap to the requested slot within a large swap entry before allocating a folio. If allocation or charging fails, the error path compares this adjusted value with the original entry still stored in the XArray in shmem_confirm_swap().
Unless the index is at the start of the entry, this turns -ENOMEM into -EEXIST even though nothing changed.
The caller retries -EEXIST, so persistent allocation failures can leave the task spinning instead of returning the error.
Restore swap to index_entry on allocation failure so the existing error path checks the original entry. This preserves the allocation error if the entry is unchanged and still retries if it changed concurrently.

item.title: CVE-2026-99736
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
mm/shmem: fix accounting of swapin-error markers
A failed swap read replaces the swap entry with a swapin-error marker in the page-cache and subtracts its pages from "alloced" and "swapped"; however, it leaves their block charge in place.
Removing the marker during truncate then subtracts from "swapped" again. This can underflow the counters or make swapped reach zero while other pages remain swapped out, causing swapoff to loop without finding them.
When installing the marker, subtract only from "swapped" and let shmem_recalc_inode() reduce "alloced" and release the block charge.
Make shmem_free_swap() report successful removal separately from the number of swap pages freed, so removing a swapin-error marker does not subtract from "swapped" again.
It's a bit confusing, but replacing a swapped out page by a swapin-error marker in shmem_set_folio_swapin_error() behaves as follows:
Initially: alloced=1, swapped=1, nrpages=0 Calling shmem_recalc_inode(inode, 0, -1) -> swapped = 0 -> freed = 1 - 0 - 0 = 1 -> alloced -= freed -> alloced=0, swapped=0, block charge released

item.title: CVE-2026-99735 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
mm/mglru: don't use stack pointers when walking PUD and PMD tables
MGLRU passes stack copies of page-table entries in walk_pud_range() and walk_pmd_range() when walking to the next level. These copies can become stale when khugepaged or MADV_DONTNEED (CONFIG_PT_RECLAIM) removes a PTE table concurrently.
This pattern dates back to commit bd74fdaea146 ("mm: multi-gen LRU: support page table walks"). Likely, earlier locking masked the latent bug. Later changes exposed it: commit 1d65b771bc08 ("mm/khugepaged: retract_page_tables() without mmap or vma lock") allowed concurrent retraction, and commit cf4a65539c13 ("memcg-v1: no need for memcg locking for MGLRU") dropped the walker's outer RCU protection.
The fix is simple, so just fix the original commit so we don't have to speculate. To fix it, pass the actual PMD/PUD pointers. This restores the RCU-protected lookup and validation against the live PMD. Note that the PUD handling is required as well to handle folded page tables correctly in all cases.
Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private.
[ david: handle walk_pud_range() as well, clarify+simplify description, adjust Fixes: ]
Score: 7.8 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-99734
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
mm/shmem: make shmem_file() check the file's inode
shmem_file() only checks if file->f_mapping is a shmem mapping. This mapping can belong to another file, however, as with a Coda file backed by a tmpfs container after mmap().
So it does not guarantee that the file inode is an actual shmem inode.
Seal handling and memfd preservation use this check before accessing shmem inode state, so they can access an inode of the wrong type.
Let's make shmem_file() check the inode's file operations instead, to identify shmem inodes reliably. This will identify regular shmem inodes, including memfds and ordinary tmpfs files, independently of wrapper file operations.
Use shmem_mapping() in collapse_file() instead to not change the behavior of collapse_file(): it operates on the page cache and uses mapping->host for shmem inode operations. Focusing on the file does not seem relevant.

item.title: CVE-2026-99732
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
mm/filemap: read mapping->a_ops->free_folio under i_lock
memory_failure() -> ... -> filemap_remove_folio() can read mapping->a_ops after the inode has been freed. Once the folio is deleted from the pagecache it no longer pins the mapping, so after i_lock is dropped e.g., a concurrent final iput() can evict and free the inode before filemap_free_folio() looks up mapping->a_ops->free_folio.
Most callers hold a reference on the inode, but not all.
Documentation/filesystems/vfs.rst explicitly states that ->free_folio() must not assume the original address_space mapping still exists.
Fix it by loading ->free_folio while i_lock is still held, similar to what folio_unmap_invalidate() does.
Inline filemap_free_folio() into its remaining caller such that delete_from_page_cache_batch() also just loads the callback before dropping the i_lock.
The bug was found by code inspection and has not been reproduced.
Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private.
[ david: get rid of filemap_free_folio() entirely; improve patch description ]

item.title: CVE-2026-99731
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
mm/filemap: don't lose a folio lock wakeup to a signal
An exclusive waiter in folio_wait_bit_common() can leave the wait loop because of a fatal signal, then be woken by folio_unlock() before finish_wait(). If the waker did not hand over the lock, the waiter returns -EINTR without trying to acquire it.
folio_wake_bit() stops after waking the first exclusive waiter, so this loses the wakeup and can leave other waiters asleep indefinitely on an unlocked folio.
After finish_wait(), let a waiter woken without a lock handoff try once more to acquire the lock. If successful, return success so the caller's eventual unlock wakes the next waiter. Otherwise, the current lock owner will do so.
Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private.
[ david: clarify and simplify comment + description ]

item.title: CVE-2026-99730 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
mm/filemap: finish fault cleanup before dropping the fault lock
On a retried fault, a fatal signal interrupting the folio lock wait makes lock_folio_maybe_drop_mmap() drop the fault lock without pinning the file. However, filemap_fault() may still need to release mapping->invalidate_lock. A concurrent munmap() can release the last file reference and free the mapping before that unlock.
Defer dropping the fault lock to filemap_fault()'s retry cleanup, after releasing invalidate_lock. If the fault lock was already dropped for I/O, release the existing file reference instead. Keep the fault lock held for FAULT_FLAG_RETRY_NOWAIT as before.
Score: 7.8 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-99729
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
mm/rmap: handle device-exclusive entries in folio_referenced_one()
page_vma_mapped_walk() can return non-present device-exclusive entries, but folio_referenced_one() passes them to PTE young-bit accessors that require present PTEs.
We must neither call clear_flush_young_ptes_notify() nor folio_pte_batch() with non-present entries. For example, clearing the young bit on non-present PTEs can corrupt the entry: on arm64 PTE_AF overlaps the swap type, so clearing it turns a device-exclusive entry into an ordinary swap entry.
folio_pte_batch() will VM_WARN_ON_FOLIO.
Apply the same approach as the previous fixes to e.g., damon_ptep_mkold(): treat these entries as old from the CPU's perspective and obtain their young state through the MMU notifier.
Skip PTE batching and MGLRU look-around for non-present entries, and don't modify non-present PTEs.

item.title: CVE-2026-99727
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
mm/huge_memory: properly handle refcounted PUD mappings on fork
copy_huge_pud() copies device-DAX entries without taking a folio reference or updating mapcounts and the child's RSS.
For example, MADV_GUARD_INSTALL sets VM_MAYBE_GUARD on a device-DAX VMA, forcing copy_page_range() to traverse the whole VMA on fork. Any remaining huge PUDs are then copied without accounting for the new mappings. Unmapping them in the child decrements accounting that was never added.
Use vm_normal_page_pud() to identify refcounted mappings. Take a folio reference and add the child's PUD rmap and RSS accounting before installing the copied entry. Pass src and dst VMAs consistently instead of src and dst MM. Move the TODO.

item.title: CVE-2026-99723
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
vhost-vdpa: fix pinned page leak in vhost_vdpa_pa_map() error path
When pin_user_pages() or vhost_vdpa_map() fails, vhost_vdpa_pa_map() is supposed to unpin the pages pinned after the last successfully mapped chunk, i.e. the range [map_pfn, last_pfn]. The unpin is guarded by nchunks, but nchunks is reset to 0 every time a chunk is mapped from inside the current page list, so a failure after any such boundary leaves that pending range pinned forever. With physically scattered memory nearly every page list contains a boundary, so the leak happens on practically every failed IOTLB update.
The pending range is non-empty exactly when a page has been pinned, which last_pfn already tells us, so drop nchunks and test last_pfn.

item.title: CVE-2026-99722
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
vringh: bound top-level re-entry into indirect tables
In __vringh_iov(), the F_INDIRECT branch descends into the indirect table and continues before the descriptor accounting runs. A top-level indirect descriptor is therefore never charged to count. If such a descriptor sets NEXT to point back at itself, returning from the indirect table resumes at the same top-level descriptor, which is again not counted, so the walk never makes forward progress.
Because count stays flat and indirect_count is reset to 0 on every return to the top-level table, neither bound in the loop check trips. A guest can spin the vringh worker at 100% CPU inside __vringh_iov(), an uninterruptible host DoS.
Move the descriptor accounting above the indirect switch so that a top-level indirect descriptor is charged one top-level traversal step before the walk descends into its table, bringing this re-entry under the existing vrh->vring.num bound. Each top-level descriptor is still charged at most one step and indirect_count still bounds a single table, so legitimate chains (including the multiple-indirect case in tools/virtio/vringh_test.c) stay within vring.num, while a cyclic indirect descriptor is now rejected with -ELOOP.

item.title: CVE-2026-99721
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
hwmon: (aquacomputer_d5next) reject short status reports
The HID raw_event callback runs before HID core validates the received report length. aqc_raw_event() reads device-specific status fields at fixed offsets, including multi-byte values, without first ensuring that the received buffer contains every field. A truncated report can therefore cause out-of-bounds reads and update hwmon state with unrelated data.
The required length differs between supported devices and cannot be derived from the HID report descriptor. Define the minimum length needed by each asynchronous status format, select it while configuring the device, and reject reports that do not contain the last field accessed by that format. Keep the published length zero until probe configuration is complete, which also excludes legacy devices whose status is retrieved through feature reports.

item.title: CVE-2026-99720
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
hwmon: chipcap2: fix IRQ teardown ordering
The threaded IRQs are currently requested before the hwmon device is registered. Since devres releases resources in reverse order, the hwmon device is unregistered before the IRQs are freed during driver teardown. An IRQ may therefore still run after the hwmon device has been released and access the stale data->hwmon pointer.
Separate IRQ discovery from IRQ registration so that the IRQ numbers and alarm visibility flags are initialized before registering the hwmon device while the IRQs are released before the hwmon device during devres cleanup.

item.title: CVE-2026-99719
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
hwmon: (lm87) Fix drvdata type confusion in vrm_show() and vrm_store()
When an LM87 or ADM1024 device is probed with VID support enabled, reading from or writing to the vrm sysfs attribute triggers a driver data type confusion in vrm_show() and vrm_store() in drivers/hwmon/lm87.c.
In lm87_probe(), the driver stores the struct lm87_data pointer on the I2C client via i2c_set_clientdata() and passes the struct i2c_client pointer as the drvdata argument to devm_hwmon_device_register_with_groups(), which attaches the attribute groups to the registered hwmon device with client as its driver_data. Unlike the other sysfs callbacks that retrieve client via dev_get_drvdata() and then obtain data via i2c_get_clientdata(), vrm_show() and vrm_store() assign dev_get_drvdata(dev) directly to struct lm87_data *. Dereferencing data->vrm therefore accesses the struct i2c_client instance at offsetof(struct lm87_data, vrm), causing vrm_show() to leak an unrelated byte from struct i2c_client to userspace and vrm_store() to corrupt a byte within struct i2c_client while failing to update the actual VRM value.
Fix the problem by assigning the return value from dev_get_drvdata(dev) to struct i2c_client *client and using i2c_get_clientdata() to get the actual client data.

item.title: CVE-2026-99718
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
hwmon: (peci/dimmtemp) Fix devres leak and UAF on concurrent unbind
When a peci_dimmtemp device is unbound concurrently with its delayed initialization work (detect_work), newly allocated devm resources and the hwmon device are leaked, leading to a use-after-free when reading the lingering hwmon sysfs attributes.
In peci_dimmtemp_probe(), detect_work is registered for cancellation via devm_delayed_work_autocancel(). During driver detach, devres_release_all() first moves all existing entries from dev->devres_head onto a local todo list before invoking their release callbacks in reverse order. If create_dimm_temp_info_delayed() is already running when devm_delayed_work_drop() calls cancel_delayed_work_sync(), create_dimm_temp_info() can allocate dimmtemp_label strings via devm_kzalloc()/devm_kasprintf() and register the hwmon device via devm_hwmon_device_register_with_info(), appending new devres entries to the now-empty dev->devres_head. Once the work finishes, devres_release_all() frees priv and priv->name from the local todo list without re-evaluating dev->devres_head, leaving the late devres allocations and registered hwmon device behind with a dangling priv pointer.
Cancel detect_work synchronously in a driver .remove() callback instead of relying on devm_delayed_work_autocancel() so that the work is fully drained before devres_release_all() detaches dev->devres_head, allowing any devm resources registered by the delayed work to be released in proper reverse order. Also only schedule detect_work when check_populated_dimms() returns -EAGAIN so that probe failure paths do not leave delayed work pending.

item.title: CVE-2026-99717
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
hwmon: (pmbus/q54sj108a2) Add missing NULL pointer check
When CONFIG_DEBUG_FS is enabled and per-client PMBus debugfs directory creation fails during pmbus_do_probe(), q54sj108a2_probe() passes the NULL pointer returned by pmbus_get_debugfs_dir() to debugfs_create_dir() without validation, creating its debugfs directory at the debugfs root instead of under the client directory.
If pmbus_init_debugfs() fails to create the client directory, data->debugfs is left as NULL or an ERR_PTR, which pmbus_get_debugfs_dir() converts to NULL. Passing a NULL parent to debugfs_create_dir() places q54sj108a2_dir in the root of the debugfs filesystem and populates it with attribute files whose private data pointers reference psu->debugfs_entries. Because this root-level directory is outside the client debugfs hierarchy, PMBus core cleanup does not remove it on device unbind, leaking the debugfs entries and causing a use-after-free of the devm-allocated struct q54sj108a2_data if the orphaned files are accessed via q54sj108a2_debugfs_read() or q54sj108a2_debugfs_write() after device removal.
Fix the problem by adding the missing NULL pointer check.

item.title: CVE-2026-99716
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
hwmon: (coretemp) Set nr_cores only after core_data allocation succeeds
In init_temp_data(), pdata->nr_cores is populated from topology_num_cores_per_package() before allocating pdata->core_data. If that allocation fails, init_temp_data() returns NULL with pdata->core_data still NULL and pdata->nr_cores set to a positive value.
coretemp_add_core() logs the error without failing coretemp_cpu_online(), so the CPU still comes online with pdata->hwmon_dev registered. When the CPU is later taken offline (or the module is unloaded), coretemp_cpu_offline() calls get_temp_data(pd, cpu), which loops up to pdata->nr_cores and dereferences the NULL pdata->core_data pointer.
Store the core count in a local variable and assign pdata->nr_cores only after pdata->core_data is allocated, preserving the invariant that pdata->nr_cores is zero whenever pdata->core_data is NULL.

item.title: CVE-2026-99713
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
KVM: x86/mmu: Conditionally resched when retrying gPTE walk on A/D update failure
Conditionally reschedule when retrying a guest PTE walk because the CMPXCHG to update A/D bits failed, e.g. because a different task/vCPU modified the relevant gPTEs. On kernels without involuntary preemption of some kind, a misbehaving guest can "capture" a pCPU effectively indefinitely and trigger soft lockups by continuously modifying its gPTEs such that the result of the walk is remains valid.

item.title: CVE-2026-99712
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
KVM: x86: Conditionally resched when restarting REP string emulation
When restarting emulation, e.g. of a REP-prefixed string instruction, conditionally reschedule as emulating guest writes can be deceptively slow and expensive, e.g. when shadow paging is in use and each write can trigger write tracking.
In a perfect world, restarting emulation (or not) would be less arbitrary, e.g. would honor not only host events (NEED_RESCHED, signals, etc.) but also guest events (e.g. by checking kvm_vcpu_has_events()). Unfortunately, as pointed out by Sashiko, pio_in_emulated()'s read-ahead logic is baked into the restart logic, as KVM relies on restarting emulation to drain the cache and avoid duplicate reads from the I/O port. I.e. re-entering the guest on kvm_vcpu_has_events() or __xfer_to_guest_mode_work_pending() would introduce architecturally-incorrect, guest-visible changes.

item.title: CVE-2026-99711
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
KVM: nVMX: Process each host MSR entry at most once when unwinding failed VM-Entry
Add a missing "break" in the inner for-loop of the open coded mess that unwinds MSRs back to the pre-VM-Enter state when VMLAUNCH/VMRESUME VM-Fails due to a consistency check that is caught by hardware but missed by KVM. I.e. move on to the next MSR in the VM-Entry load list after performing a write using a value found in the VM-Exit load list. Processing *every* matching entry in the VM-Exit load list makes the processing quadratic, which is problematic if the load lists are full of MSRs that are expensive to emulate. E.g. writing APIC_BASE triggers kvm_recalculate_apic_map() and a whole pile of unnecessary work.
Functionally, arbitrarily restoring the value of the first matching entry is "fine", because none of this is architecturally correct: the load lists are never supposed to have been used in the first place. In practice, it's likely a moot point as no well-behaved VMM will have multiple, diverging entries in the load lists.

item.title: CVE-2026-99710
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
KVM: x86/mmu: Cap number of parent PTEs per SP at 1000 (the arbitrary rmap limit)
When potentially reusing a shadow page, zap the shadow page if its number of parent PTEs exceeds KVM's (mostly) arbitrary rmap recycling threshold. Letting the guest create a (mostly) unbounded number of parent PTEs allows the guest to coerce KVM into creating lists containing millions of PTEs, effectively bounded only by the maximum number of shadow pages.
Because PTE lists are simple singly linked lists, removal is O(n). Even worse, if a list is constructed just so, teardown can be O(n^2), e.g. if SPTEs are built such that zapping child SPTEs always zaps the last entry in the list. To cap things off, all paths that walk PTE lists do so while holding mmu_lock, without conditionally rescheduling.
Using a doubly linked list would not address the issue, as removal would remain O(n) since KVM still wouldn't know where in the list to remove from. Removal could be made O(1) by storing a per-SPTE pointer, but that would largely defeat the purpose of reusing SPs, and would penalize well-behaved guests, especially for nested TDP where aliasing page tables is uncommon.
So, cap the maximum number of parent PTEs at the rmap limit. In practice, well-behaved guests will likely never run afoul of the limit. E.g. when running Linux as L1 with TDP, the number of parent PTEs for a single SP tops out at under 200 (though undoubtedly obscure workloads can push it higher). Deliberately use a "greater than or equal" as opposed to rmap's strictly "greater than", as the rmap code checks the threshold immediately *after* inserting into the list, i.e. the limit is 1000 for rmaps, KVM just very briefly blows past it.
Apply the check to both indirect and direct SPs, because while a fully direct MMU naturally limits the number of parent PTEs to '1', direct SPs in indirect MMUs have no such constraint. E.g. if the guest maps a huge PTE into many locations in its page tables, and KVM is backing the hugepage with a direct SP, i.e. with a series of smaller pages, then KVM could end up with a direct SP with many parents.
Note, shadow_mmu_try_split_huge_pages() always restarts the rmap walk or bails entirely if it gets to the point where it tries to grab a SP, i.e. there is *no* pre-existing bug that would be tripped by zapping a SP and thus rmaps when getting a SP.

item.title: CVE-2026-99709
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
inet: frags: limit the truesize of a reassembly queue
The truesize of fragments in a reassembly queue is only bounded by the per netns ipfrag_high_thresh sysctl, which has no upper limit.
inet_frag_reasm_finish() sums the truesize of all fragments in an int. If this sum reaches 2^32, it wraps, and the final sk_wmem_alloc adjustment of the socket owning the reassembled skb can cancel its own reference, leading to a use-after-free of this socket.
This can be triggered from an unprivileged user/network namespace, raising ipfrag_high_thresh and using padded TUN packets, which keep a large truesize after being trimmed by ip_rcv_core().
Track the sum of the truesize of fragments in each queue, and refuse a fragment that would make it bigger than INT_MAX / 2. Callers kill the queue on this error. This bound is far above the needs of legitimate traffic.

item.title: CVE-2026-99707 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
mm/khugepaged: flush deferred unmaps before dropping a failed folio
collapse_file() can fail its reference-count or dirty-folio check after unmapping with TTU_BATCH_FLUSH. Both paths put back the isolated folio, then unlock it and drop the lookup reference before reaching the common try_to_unmap_flush().
The page-cache reference does not keep the folio stable once the lock is released. Another collapse can replace and free it. With its PTEs already gone, that collapse cannot flush the first task's per-task TLB batch, and retract_page_tables() skips short or unaligned VMAs. A CPU can therefore retain a user translation to the freed folio. This has been reproduced with unprivileged MADV_COLLAPSE on a memfd.
Flush at out_unlock while the lookup reference and folio lock are still held. The common flush continues to cover the accumulated pagelist on both success and rollback, preserving batching on successful collapses.
Score: 7.8 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-99706
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
mm: fix address wraparound when scanning large folio PTEs
numa_rebuild_large_mapping() and do_swap_page() can be tricked into generating an address wraparound, crashing the kernel. All that's required is to map a tail page of a large folio close enough to the start/end of the address space to e.g., make
unsigned long addr_start = addr - (nr << PAGE_SHIFT);
to wrap around.
Let's fix it by providing a better helper, folio_scan_range(), that takes care of staying within VMA and page table boundaries while handling possible wraparounds.
There are some nasty details, like not being able to use pmd_addr_end() in this context. Add some helpful comments for these cases.

item.title: CVE-2026-99704
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
mm/page-writeback: avoid 32-bit overflow in dirty threshold shares
The ratios used by __wb_calc_thresh() are scaled to parts per million, but the threshold and ratio operands are unsigned long. On 32-bit kernels, their multiplication can wrap before the result is assigned to u64.
For example, with a threshold of 25600 pages and the default maximum ratio of 1000000, wb_max_thresh becomes 4125 pages instead of 25600. The shared threshold and minimum share calculations can overflow in the same way, producing incorrect per-writeback dirty limits.
Use a u64 threshold for the three ratio multiplications and div_u64() to retain the existing division order and rounding.

item.title: CVE-2026-99703
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
mm/hugetlb: fix mremap deadlock when PMD sharing is possible
move_hugetlb_page_tables() holds the mapping's i_mmap_rwsem for write while moving hugetlb PTEs. This prevents races with truncation and protects huge_pmd_unshare(), but the move loop must not call helpers that can acquire the same rwsem for read.
huge_pte_alloc() can do that when the destination can use PMD sharing: it may call huge_pmd_share(), which takes i_mmap_rwsem for read while searching for a shareable PMD table. Calling it while the move path already holds i_mmap_rwsem for write can deadlock.
Avoid that path for PMD-sized hugetlb mappings that can use PMD sharing. Instead of allocating or sharing the destination page table while moving, zap the source range and let the destination fault path populate or share the PMD lazily.
Reuse the hugetlb unmap logic for the source-side zap by splitting the core loop out of __unmap_hugepage_range(). The wrapper keeps the existing tlb_start_vma(), tlb_end_vma() and huge_pmd_unshare_flush() behavior, while move_hugetlb_page_tables() can reuse the unmap loop with its existing mmu_gather.

item.title: CVE-2026-99698
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
mm/cma: accept memory of CMA areas reserved at a fixed address
CMA areas allocated from memblock have their memory accepted by memblock_alloc_range_nid(), but areas reserved at a fixed address with memblock_reserve() are not.
If a fixed CMA area is requested by the cma=<size>@<base> command line parameter, it may be in regular RAM and on TDX and SEV-SNP guests it must be accepted.
Accept the memory of fixed CMA areas as well, so that all CMA areas are accepted regardless of how they were reserved.

item.title: CVE-2026-99697 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
mm: memcontrol: fix NULL pointer deref and UAF from high_work_func() on dying memcg
When memory.high is exceeded in non-task context, try_charge_memcg() schedules memcg->high_work without taking a reference on the memcg, and high_work_func() invokes reclaim_high() without pinning the memcg.
With obj_cgroup reparenting, introduced in commit bf4f059954dc ("mm: memcg/slab: obj_cgroup API"), objects charged to a child memcg are reparented to its parent in mem_cgroup_css_offline() instead of holding a reference on the child until uncharged. Subsequent uncharges of those objects go to the parent, which can leave the child's memory use permanently above its high limit, so any later charge on the offlined memcg in non-task context schedules high_work. This was later widened from kernel memory to LRU folios when commit f1cf8d2f36dc ("mm: memcontrol: eliminate the problem of dying memory cgroup for LRU folios") converted LRU folios to use obj_cgroup reparenting.
cancel_work_sync(&memcg->high_work) only runs at the end of teardown in mem_cgroup_css_free(), so high_work_func() can start or still be running reclaim_high() after mem_cgroup_css_released() or shrink_many() has called lru_gen_release_memcg() and unhashed lruvec->lrugen.list. If reclaim tries to rotate the memcg, lru_gen_rotate_memcg() dereferences a NULL pprev pointer. This issue is specific to MGLRU and was introduced with the memcg LRU in commit e4dde56cd208 ("mm: multi-gen LRU: per-node lru_gen_folio lists").
With either traditional LRU or MGLRU, css_free_rwork_fn() calls css_rstat_exit() which frees per-CPU rstat data before calling mem_cgroup_css_free(). If reclaim_high() is still running, rstat updates via mod_lruvec_state() -> __css_rstat_updated() cause a use-after-free on the per-CPU rstat data. This was introduced when commit 5da3bfa029d6 ("cgroup: use separate rstat trees for each subsystem") moved css_rstat_exit() ahead of ss->css_free().
Fix both problems by acquiring a reference with css_tryget_online() in high_work_func() before calling reclaim_high(), and by resetting memory.high and swap.high to PAGE_COUNTER_MAX in mem_cgroup_css_offline() so that charges via references on an offlined memcg do not trigger high_work on the dead child and skip checking live ancestors in try_charge_memcg().
Acquiring the reference in high_work_func() rather than before scheduling high_work is safe because mem_cgroup_css_free() calls irq_work_sync() and cancel_work_sync() which cancels pending work and waits for an already running high_work_func() to complete before mem_cgroup_free() frees the memcg. css_tryget_online() uses percpu_ref_tryget_live() and is safe to call after percpu_ref_exit() before the cgroup is freed unlike css_tryget().
