item.title: CVE-2026-99696
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ocfs2: find the xattr entry again after defragmenting a bucket
ocfs2_xattr_set_entry_bucket() hands loc.xl_entry to ocfs2_xa_set() twice: once for the bucket as it stands, and, if that reports -ENOSPC, once more after ocfs2_defrag_xattr_bucket() has packed the name/value pairs down.
Defragmenting ends by sorting the entry array on xe_name_hash. Buckets are kept sorted, so the sort only permutes entries that share a hash, but lib/sort.c is an unstable heapsort and it does permute them. loc.xl_entry is an address inside xh_entries[], so afterwards it denotes whichever entry landed in that slot rather than the one the search found.
The second ocfs2_xa_set() then works on the wrong entry. Nothing on that path compares the entry's name with xi->xi_name, so what happens depends on how the two entries compare in size: ocfs2_xa_reuse_entry() trips its BUG_ON() when the padded name sizes differ, and otherwise the new value is written into the neighbouring attribute's value slot while the attribute being set is left untouched. setxattr() reports success either way.
Remember the entry's hash before defragmenting and look the entry up again afterwards, the way ocfs2_xattr_bucket_find() does. An entry that cannot be found again means the bucket no longer holds what the search found, so fail with -EFSCORRUPTED rather than writing through the stale pointer.

item.title: CVE-2026-99695
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ocfs2: find the xattr entry again after converting a block to a bucket
ocfs2_xattr_create_index_block() turns a non-indexed xattr block into a tree by copying it into a bucket, and the copy sorts the entries: a block holds them in insertion order, a bucket by name hash. ocfs2_xattr_update_xattr_search() nevertheless relocates the caller's search by the index the entry had in the block, so unless the two orders agreed it points at an unrelated entry, and nothing between there and the write compares that entry's name with the one being set.
Setting an xattr whose new value no longer fits the block arrives here with xs->not_found clear. The block gave up because ocfs2_xa_block_can_reuse() wants an exact namevalue size match, while ocfs2_xa_bucket_can_reuse() only wants an entry at least as large as the new one, so the bucket accepts a pair the block rejected and the update lands on whichever entry the sort left at that index. Equal padded name lengths get that other attribute's value replaced in place and its name left alone, so setxattr returns success while the attribute asked for keeps its old value. A longer one trips ocfs2_xa_reuse_entry()'s BUG_ON, and a shorter one is refused by the bucket as well, so ocfs2_xa_prepare_entry() wipes the entry and writes the new name over it, leaving xe_name_hash describing a name that is no longer there.
Find the entry again by the name being set, matching the type as well. The copy carries every entry and every name over unchanged, and (type, name) pairs are unique within a block, so the match is exact. The type matters because the handlers strip their prefix before calling ocfs2_xattr_set(), so user.foo and trusted.foo share a stored name, a stored length and a hash, and both can sit in the same block.
The name has to come from xi rather than from xs->here: a failed set can remove the entry xs->here names, and only the "growing" caller sets ctxt->set_abort, which is what stops the conversion. Scan every entry rather than narrowing on the hash the way ocfs2_find_xe_in_bucket() does, since an existing entry keeps the hash it was stored under, which a kernel that sign-extended the name bytes made different from the one computed now. An empty result means the entry did not survive the failed set and this has become an insert; leaving xs->here alone would keep it pointing into the block, which is rewritten as a tree root before the caller reads it again.

item.title: CVE-2026-99694
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ocfs2: do not index before the entry array when dividing an empty bucket
ocfs2_divide_xattr_bucket() appends an empty bucket carrying a sentinel hash when the source bucket has no divide position, taking that hash from xh_entries[start - 1]. ocfs2_xattr_find_divide_pos() returns count when every entry shares one hash, and its loop does not run at all for count < 2, so an empty bucket comes back with start == count == 0 and the read is xh_entries[-1].
That is outside the __counted_by_le(xh_count) bounds of xh_entries[] and lands on the header, so the value picked up is xh_count | xh_free_start << 16. One above it is written into the new bucket's xh_entries[0] and committed, which leaves a bucket whose first hash does not follow the bucket before it. ocfs2_xattr_bucket_find() binary searches on xh_entries[0], so the broken key hides the range the sentinel was meant to cover: getxattr() answers -ENODATA for an attribute that is stored, and an insert can go to the wrong bucket and leave two copies of a name. The cross cluster divide hands the same value back as a tree record's e_cpos, which then claims a hash range it does not cover.
Read xh_entries[0] instead. The branch is only reached when every entry shares one hash, so for a non-empty bucket it holds the same value, and for an empty one it is the slot that carries the bucket key.
An empty bucket reaches the divide from ocfs2_check_xattr_bucket_collision(), which reports no collision for one, through ocfs2_add_new_xattr_bucket() and ocfs2_extend_xattr_bucket(). It does not take a failed set to get there: a divide that finds no position is itself what leaves an empty sentinel bucket behind, and a later extend can pick it as the target.

item.title: CVE-2026-99693
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ocfs2/dlm: serialize migration MLE cleanup on failure
A migration MLE has a base reference for the mastering answer and an in-use reference held by dlm_migrate_lockres(). The finishing assertion consumes the base reference, but migration failure drops it again without checking whether the assertion already consumed it.
The target queues its migration worker before it acknowledges the ALL_DONE packet, so its finishing assertion can be handled while the sender still waits for the status. If the connection fails before the status arrives, dlm_send_one_lockres() returns an error for a migration that the target has already completed:
Old-master sender Finishing assertion ----------------- ------------------- publish MLE; take in-use reference send ALL_DONE; wait for status take lookup reference unlink MLE put lookup and base references send returns a connection error put base reference again; free MLE put in-use reference; access freed MLE
dlm_assert_master_handler() holds dlm->spinlock from the MLE lookup to the final puts, and it takes dlm->master_lock around the unlink and the puts. Decide under the same locks: if the MLE is already unhashed, the assertion consumed the base reference, so drop only the sender's in-use reference. Otherwise unlink it before consuming the base reference so a later assertion no longer finds it.
An assertion that got there first has also made the target the owner and cleared DLM_LOCK_RES_MIGRATING. Treating the attempt as failed at that point would leave the lockres owned by the target while this node still holds the other nodes' locks and refmap bits, so it could neither be purged nor migrated again. Finish our side as a completed migration does instead: drop those locks under res->spinlock if the target still owns the lockres, and recalculate its usage.
Use the same cleanup for the pre-send failure, the send failure and the target-death failure paths. The sender's in-use reference keeps the MLE alive until its final put outside the nested locks. Successful migration retains its existing in-use-only put.
A target that has died cannot assert after the sender has seen its death. The o2net node-down callback runs before the DLM one; it disconnects the node and flushes the workqueue that runs the message handlers, so an assertion already received has been handled by the time the DLM removes the node from the domain map. A node that leaves the domain cleanly sends its exit message only after its assertions have been answered.
Two windows of the hand-over itself are left as they are: the handler switches the owner and the sender drops the other nodes' locks moments later, and an assertion from a live target that arrives after the sender has given up still meets the owner check in the handler. Waiting for the target before giving up would only stretch the first window into the time in which recovery of the target can observe it.

item.title: CVE-2026-99692
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ocfs2: stop recovery before shutting down local allocators
Recovery completion needs the local allocators until it has finished reclaiming a failed node's allocation window and truncate log. During unmount, quota recovery is stopped first, but that leaves recovery_state at OCFS2_REC_QUOTA_DISABLED. New non-quota recovery can still start.
ocfs2_truncate_log_shutdown() drains existing completion work and releases osb_tl_bh before ocfs2_recovery_exit() closes that publication path:
Unmount Recovery ------- -------- stop quota recovery; disable quotas truncate_log_shutdown() flush existing completion work recover another failed node queue completion flush local log; release buffer complete_truncate_log_recovery() use released osb_tl_bh recovery_exit(): disable and drain
An extra buffer reference alone would still let completion append new records after the final truncate-log flush.
Split stopping and draining recovery from freeing its state. Stop all recovery producers and drain completion work before shutting down either local allocator. Keep recovery-state release at its existing later point, so its lifetime relative to other teardown users stays unchanged. The second stop at recovery_exit() is harmless once recovery is disabled.

item.title: CVE-2026-99691
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ocfs2/cluster: unlink socket containers before releasing resources
A socket container's node and socket must remain alive while the container is on sock_containers. The debugfs formatter reads sc_node and sc_sock under o2net_debug_lock without taking their references, but sc_kref_release() releases both before taking that lock to unlink the container.
With CONFIG_DEBUG_FS enabled, a synchronous sender can retain its last socket-container reference after o2net_disconnect_node() has detached the connection and flushed o2net_wq. The caller runs outside that workqueue. After the sender removes its configfs dependency, node removal can proceed without waiting for the sender's final sc_put():
Sender (final sc_put) Configfs rmdir Debugfs reader -------------------- -------------- -------------- o2nm_undepend_item() Drop node item refs o2nm_node_put() [node can be freed] sc_seq_show() Lock debug lock Read sc_node->nd_name Unlock debug lock sc_node = NULL o2net_debug_del_sc()
The earlier socket release has a similar window. The container is still selectable while its socket has been released and sc_sock has not yet been cleared:
Sender (final sc_put) Debugfs reader -------------------- -------------- sock_release(sc->sc_sock) [socket can be freed] sc_seq_show() Lock debug lock Read sc_sock->sk fields Unlock debug lock sc_sock = NULL ... o2net_debug_del_sc()
Move o2net_debug_del_sc() before releasing either resource. Unlinking under the existing debug lock waits for an active formatter to finish and prevents later readers from selecting the container. This covers both socket fields and node fields, including nd_num in the stats formatter.

item.title: CVE-2026-99690 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ocfs2: cache the mount context for dentry lock callbacks
ocfs2_drop_dentry_lock() drops the inode reference before releasing the DENTRY lock. This lets inode eviction release the local inode and open locks before a remote unlink can proceed past the DENTRY lock.
A DLM callback can still arrive before the DENTRY lock has been dropped. ocfs2_get_dentry_osb() obtains the mount context through dl_inode->i_sb, which can access a freed inode when the downconvert thread drops the last inode reference in its post-unlock callback:
Downconvert thread DLM callback thread ------------------ ------------------- ocfs2_process_blocked_lock() ocfs2_dentry_post_unlock() ocfs2_dentry_lock_put() ocfs2_drop_dentry_lock() iput(dl->dl_inode) [inode reclaimed after RCU] ocfs2_blocking_ast() ocfs2_get_dentry_osb() dl->dl_inode->i_sb ocfs2_simple_drop_lockres()
Store the mount context in the DENTRY lock resource's l_priv field and use the default mount-context lookup. Recover the containing dentry lock with container_of(), as already done for refcount locks, and remove ocfs2_get_dentry_osb(). ocfs2_dismount_volume() shuts down the DLM before freeing the mount context, so callbacks can use it without accessing the inode. Preserve the existing iput-before-unlock order to avoid delaying local inode and open lock release until after the DENTRY lock is released.
Score: 7.8 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-99689
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
xfs: fix temporary cursor leak in btree shift corruption paths
In xfs_btree_lshift and xfs_btree_rshift, when XFS_IS_CORRUPT detects an invalid firstrec/lastrec result after xfs_btree_dup_cursor has successfully allocated a temporary cursor, the error path jumps to error0 which returns without freeing tcur. This leaks the cursor memory, the xfs_group reference, and the per-level buffer references held by the duplicated cursor. Jump to error1 instead, which calls xfs_btree_del_cursor(tcur, XFS_BTREE_ERROR) to properly release all resources.

item.title: CVE-2026-99688 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
net/sched: sch_qfq: prevent aggregate self-replacement
qfq_change_class() snapshots the current aggregate settings while holding the qdisc tree lock, but drops the lock before selecting the destination aggregate. During that gap, qfq_enqueue() can move the class to an aggregate matching the requested settings.
When qfq_change_class() resumes, qfq_find_agg() then returns cl->agg. If it is a singleton, qfq_deact_rm_from_agg() frees the aggregate before qfq_add_to_agg() immediately accesses the same pointer, causing a use-after-free.
While holding the tree lock, skip the replacement when the destination is already the current aggregate. Any estimator replacement has already completed, so the class change can finish normally.
Score: 7.8 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-99687
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
vhost-scsi: zero misaligned I/O bounce pages
The misaligned I/O fallback copies the full bounce scatterlist to the request buffer during completion. If a data-in command transfers less than requested, part of a newly allocated bounce page can remain unwritten.
Allocate bounce pages with __GFP_ZERO so all bytes copied during completion have a defined value. This path is already the slow fallback for misaligned I/O, so the added initialization cost is acceptable.
Found during an LLM-assisted source audit and validated with a QEMU/KVM vhost-scsi target using misaligned data-in commands.

item.title: CVE-2026-99685 [CVSS:3.1 8.4 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
iommu/virtio: Reset device before deleting virtqueues on probe failure
viommu_probe() marks the device DRIVER_OK before populating the event virtqueue and registering the IOMMU device in sysfs. viommu_fill_evtq() hands the device a set of device-writable buffers through virtqueue_add_inbuf(), so from that point on the device may write into them and into the rings.
If either step fails, the error path deletes the virtqueues without resetting the device first. The event buffers are allocated with devm_kmalloc_array() and are released as probe unwinds, so the device can go on writing to memory that has been freed.
Reset the device before deleting the virtqueues, the way viommu_remove() already does.
Score: 8.4 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-99684
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
hwrng: virtio - prevent use-after-free after a failed restore
remove_common() frees the driver data during freeze, but does not clear vdev->priv, which points to freed memory. If probe_common() then fails during restore, a later remove or freeze can dereference the dangling pointer.
Clear vdev->priv on the probe_common() error cleanup path and before freeing the driver data in remove_common(). Also reset the device and return early from remove_common() if vdev->priv is already NULL for a safe teardown after a failed restore.

item.title: CVE-2026-99683
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
vduse: fix VA/PA confusion in the coherent page fault path
vduse_domain_get_coherent_page() assumes that iotlb entries above bounce_size were installed by vduse_domain_alloc_coherent(), so it treats map->addr as a physical address. But vduse registers with use_va = true, and when the device is bound to vhost_vdpa, vhost_vdpa_va_map() stores a userspace virtual address in map->addr, which vduse_domain_set_map() then copies into the same iotlb. A process holding the domain file descriptor across a rebind can therefore fault in an arbitrary physical page with read/write access, ignoring the entry permissions.
Additionally, since the domain file mmap lacks VM_IO, the domain file itself can be mapped and passed to vhost_vdpa_va_map(), producing self-referential entries that bypass the coherent path check.
To fix, only translate entries whose backing file is the domain file itself in vduse_domain_get_coherent_page(), reject such entries in vduse_domain_set_map() since only external mappings should be imported, and set VM_IO on the domain file mmap so vhost_vdpa_va_map() refuses to map it in the first place.

item.title: CVE-2026-99682
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
virtio_blk: use synchronous quiesce in virtblk_freeze_priv()
blk_mq_run_work_fn() can call blk_mq_sched_dispatch_requests() through blk_mq_run_dispatch_ops(). The dispatcher checks QUEUE_FLAG_QUIESCED while the flag is clear. It can then be preempted before it gets a request. At that time, it has no queue usage reference, so blk_mq_freeze_queue() does not wait for it.
virtblk_freeze_priv() then calls blk_mq_quiesce_queue_nowait() and blk_mq_unfreeze_queue(). A new request can enter the queue. The old dispatcher can run again, use its old flag check, get the new request, and call virtio_queue_rq(). At the same time, virtblk_freeze_priv() can reset the device, delete the virtqueues, and free vblk->vqs. The old dispatcher can then use a deleted virtqueue or a NULL vblk->vqs, and the kernel can crash.
Fix this by using blk_mq_quiesce_queue(), which waits for dispatch code that was already running. Keep the existing freeze and unfreeze order. The queue remains quiesced until virtblk_restore_priv() calls blk_mq_unquiesce_queue().

item.title: CVE-2026-99680 [CVSS:3.1 9.4 CRITICAL]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
xfs: mark the inode preallocated for pNFS write layouts past EOF
xfs_fs_map_blocks() marks the inode XFS_DIFLAG_PREALLOC only when it allocates blocks for a write layout. A write layout past EOF can also hand out allocated blocks, such as speculative preallocation. blockgc then frees them under the layout, and another file may get them.
Mark the inode whenever a write mapping ends past EOF.
